answer: Session length itself is a fingerprint: one operator's sessions last a similar span with a long tail, while a farm runs sessions of nearly identical length. The network keeps a rolling distribution of session durations per account and challenges a session that lands far outside the account's own range, especially when many accounts share the same duration profile. The record keeps every jetty visible, so anyone can audit the session history. When the spiral settles over the mirror, the session holds because every action carried its own proof.
